headline: High: CrewAI’s default shared-memory, shell, browser, and broad egress create dangerous interaction paths with MinerU’s MCP/API document pipeline; leakage and cascading errors are plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can ingest files from its working directory and uses shared memory by default; MinerU processes untrusted PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes MCP/API surfaces. If MinerU output is copied into CrewAI inputs, prompt-like content can steer tool use. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is interaction-plausible rather than proven.
conditions: IF MinerU output is pasted or written into CrewAI-readable files
IF CrewAI agents treat extracted document text as instructions
IF an MCP or API bridge forwards MinerU text into CrewAI prompts
mitigations: Separate MinerU outputs from CrewAI prompt inputs
Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in CrewAI prompts
Disable automatic ingestion of extracted text into agent prompts
Review one sample document for prompt-like payloads before rollout

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and has broad network egress, while MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text. If both share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive document contents can flow into CrewAI’s model-provider calls. MinerU’s offline posture reduces but does not eliminate leakage because the pair still lacks isolation by default.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents in a shared directory
IF CrewAI reads those extracted files into prompts
IF CrewAI sends that context to external model providers
mitigations: Use separate directories for raw documents and agent prompts
Redact secrets before CrewAI ingestion
Run CrewAI with least-privilege network settings
Confirm MinerU outputs stay local before enabling downstream automation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; MinerU is read-only on files but exposes MCP/API interfaces. There is no evidence both write the same mutable resource or share locks, so direct write-write conflict is not established. The main overlap is operational, not a proven concurrency hazard.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same output directory
IF an external orchestrator lets CrewAI mutate files MinerU is reading
IF shared MCP tools expose the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize access to shared files with a lock
Disable CrewAI writes to MinerU input paths
Test one concurrent run on a staging workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s shared-memory crew can treat upstream text as actionable context, and MinerU produces extracted text from documents. If MinerU output is fed into CrewAI without verification, extraction errors or malicious document content can cascade into downstream actions. CrewAI’s tool-use and browser capabilities increase the blast radius beyond simple summarization.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction is used as authoritative input to CrewAI
IF CrewAI agents act on extracted facts without human review
IF browser or API tools are enabled for downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before CrewAI acts
Require citations back to source pages or cells
Disable autonomous action tools for the first deployment
Compare extracted fields against the original document on one sample

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-provided crew data and API keys, while MinerU is positioned as private/offline and document-processing. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: if regulated documents enter CrewAI’s external model calls, policy obligations may be triggered. MinerU alone is not the main compliance concern.
conditions: IF regulated documents are routed from MinerU into CrewAI model-provider calls
IF retention policies differ between the two systems
IF CrewAI logs prompts containing regulated content
mitigations: Keep regulated documents inside MinerU only
Disable prompt logging in CrewAI where possible
Document retention for both systems
Run a quick data-flow review for PHI/PII before deployment
